title: Rollback UX notes + open questions (Optimization Config safe apply/rollback)
content:
Context
- This doc is the working scratchpad for Console UX decisions: rollback confirmation copy, guardrails, partial rollout edge cases, and audit visibility.
- Feature scope: Optimization Config (batching/caching/quantization profiles) versioning + safe apply + one-click rollback.

Primary user stories (Console)
1) On-call operator (SRE / runtime on-call) sees elevated p95 after an optimization change → needs the fastest safe rollback with low cognitive load.
2) Customer admin (Dedicated/Hosted enterprise) sees regression after a config change → wants rollback but with clear blast radius and audit trace.
3) Product/security reviewer wants a clear audit trail: who rolled back, what version, why, and where.

Where rollback lives in the Console (IA)
- Optimization Configs → [Config Name] → Versions timeline
  - Each version card: version id, created by, created at, status (Draft / Validated / Applied / Promoted / Rolled back), scopes.
  - Actions per version:
    - View details
    - View diff (vs currently active)
    - Roll back to this version (only for versions that were previously known-good / promoted)
- Rollouts → Active rollouts list
  - If a rollout is in progress, rollback action is reachable from the rollout detail page as well.

Proposed rollback action model (UX-facing)
- “Rollback” means: set active pointer for the selected scope back to a prior version, and initiate an apply pipeline to converge workers.
- Not instantaneous; Console should show progress and what the system is doing.
- Rollback should be idempotent (if you click twice, the second attempt should be a no-op and show current state).

Terminology (align copy)
- Use “Rollback to version X” rather than “Revert” (security + on-call feedback: rollback is operationally familiar).
- Use “Active version” for what is currently serving.
- Use “Scope” consistently: tenant / model / region. Avoid “environment” unless it’s literally staging/prod.

Rollback CTA placement + labeling
- Version detail page: primary CTA = “Rollback to this version” (danger style)
- Timeline row: secondary action in kebab menu; avoid accidental clicks.
- If version is already active: disable CTA with tooltip “Already active for selected scope.”

Rollback confirmation modal (draft structure)
Goal: reduce mis-scoped rollbacks + make it hard to do the wrong thing quickly.

Modal title (option A)
- “Rollback optimization config?”

Modal title (option B)
- “Rollback to v{target_version}”

Body sections (proposal)
1) Summary
   - “You are about to roll back the active optimization config for the scope below. This will start an apply job to update model workers.”

2) Blast radius (must be explicit)
   - Tenant: {tenant_name / ‘All tenants’}
   - Model: {model_id}
   - Region(s): {region list}
   - Traffic coverage: {100% or canary % if partial}

3) Current → Target
   - Current active: v{current_version} (applied {timestamp})
   - Target rollback: v{target_version} (promoted {timestamp}, created by {actor})
   - Link: “View diff (current vs target)” (opens new panel, doesn’t dismiss modal)

4) Expected impact (best-effort callouts)
   - “Batching/caching settings will change.”
   - If quantization profile changes: “May change output quality; this rollback is expected to restore baseline behavior.”
   - If cache toggle changes: “Short-lived latency change may occur during cache warm-up.”

5) Safety checks / gating
   - Copy: “Rollback applies immediately. Gates will monitor error rate and latency during convergence.”
   - Open question: do we allow gating to block rollback progression? (On-call wants rollback to proceed even if gates are red; but we still want visibility if rollback itself is unhealthy.)

6) Confirmation friction (guardrail)
   - For high blast radius: require type-to-confirm “ROLLBACK” or paste the target version id.
   - For small blast radius (single tenant + single region): single click OK.
   - RBAC note: “Your role: Optimization Change Operator” (or display missing permission message + request access).

7) Required metadata (audit + operations)
   - Reason dropdown (required):
     - Latency regression
     - Elevated 5xx / timeouts
     - Quality regression (quantization)
     - Incorrect scope applied
     - Planned rollback / experiment ended
     - Other
   - Freeform text (optional but encouraged): “Notes / incident link”
   - Ticket link field (optional): “Jira/Linear URL”

Modal buttons (copy)
- Primary (danger): “Rollback now”
- Secondary: “Cancel”
- Small helper text under primary: “This starts a rollback job; it may take a few minutes to reach all workers.”

Post-confirmation UX
- After click, modal closes → show toast + route to Rollback job detail panel.
- Toast (success): “Rollback started: v{current} → v{target} for {scope}” with “View progress” link.
- If request is blocked by cooldown / concurrent apply: toast should be explicit and actionable.

Rollback job detail view (progress)
- Status: Queued / Applying / Verifying / Completed / Completed with warnings / Failed
- Progress indicators:
  - % workers converged (or shards updated)
  - Regions converged
  - Canary group status (if rollback is only for canary group)
- Metrics preview (mini-panels): p95 latency, 5xx, throughput with annotations.
- Events timeline: “Rollback requested” → “Active pointer updated” → “Workers updated” → “Verification checks passed”
- Button: “Copy rollback summary” (for incident channel)

Guardrails / constraints (proposal)
1) Cooldown
- Avoid thrash: after an apply/rollback completes, enforce a short cooldown before another change at same scope.
- Copy if blocked: “A config change was completed less than {N} minutes ago for this scope. Please wait or contact on-call lead to override.”
- Open question: who can override? SRE on-call only? feature flag?

2) Concurrency
- If an apply rollout is in progress for the same scope, and user hits rollback:
  - Option A: allow rollback, but automatically cancel/pause the rollout.
  - Option B: require user to choose: “Cancel rollout and rollback” vs “Pause rollout only”.
- Strong on-call preference (from early conversations): rollback should be the ‘big red button’ that cancels the rollout.
- We need a crisp rule that’s easy to explain.

3) Scope mismatch protection
- If user is viewing version under one scope filter but the rollback will affect a broader scope (e.g., “All regions” selected): force explicit acknowledgement.
- UI pattern: show scope selector inside modal; cannot proceed until confirmed.

4) “Known-good only” selection
- For external customers, we likely restrict rollback targets to:
  - last promoted version
  - versions that have passed validation + have been applied successfully before
- For internal, allow rollback to any validated version (behind a flag).
- Open question: do we codify a “KnownGood” marker in the Console, or infer it?

5) Partial rollout edge cases (must-handle)
A) Canary in progress (10%) and metrics are red
- User wants to roll back canary group only (return canary to baseline) vs roll back entire scope.
- Proposal: modal offers a choice:
  - “Rollback canary only (10%)” (recommended)
  - “Rollback entire rollout (100%)”
- Need PM call: is “canary only” meaningful given pointer semantics? Might require two active pointers (stable + canary). If backend doesn’t support, we should not promise it.

B) Rollout paused mid-way (e.g., 40%)
- What does rollback do?
  - Ideally: converge everything back to stable version.
  - UI must show that some shards are already on new version.
- Copy addition: “Some workers are currently serving v{new_version}. Rollback will converge all workers in this scope back to v{target_version}.”

C) Mixed state due to failure / race condition
- We should assume we can see an “inconsistent” state from the runtime.
- UI: show warning banner “Inconsistent worker state detected” with guidance: “Proceed with rollback to force convergence” + link to runbook.

6) Private deployments
- Console experience differs (customer-managed). We still want a coherent story:
  - Console should display version history and ‘desired active version’.
  - Actual convergence depends on operator apply (helm/installer).
- Copy if Private: “Rollback will update the desired config version. Your Private deployment operator will need to apply the change (helm/installer) to take effect.”
- Open question: do we show an explicit “Generate rollback command” button for Private?

Audit visibility requirements (Console)
- For each version and for each rollback action, show:
  - Who: actor (user + org), auth method if available (SSO/API token)
  - When: timestamp (UTC) + relative time
  - What: config name, version id, previous active version, target version
  - Where: tenant/model/region scope
  - Why: reason + notes + ticket link
  - Correlation: request_id / rollout_id / job_id
- Also: whether action was initiated via Console vs API.

Audit log UI: what customers should see
- Enterprise customers want to self-serve “prove it” evidence.
- Proposal:
  - Read-only Audit tab within Optimization Configs with filters (time range, actor, action type, scope).
  - Export as CSV option (or “Copy JSON payload”).
- Open question: retention shown in UI (e.g., “Audit events retained 180 days”)? Security wants this explicit.

RBAC and permission messaging
- Permissions we expect in UI:
  - View configs
  - Create/validate versions
  - Apply/promote versions
  - Rollback
  - View audit events
- UX requirement: no ambiguous “permission denied.”
  - Show: “You don’t have permission to roll back optimization configs. Ask an admin for role: Optimization Change Operator.”
  - For internal: include link to internal access request.

Copy drafts (WIP)
1) Rollback confirmation (high blast radius)
- Title: “Rollback optimization config?”
- Body: “This will roll back the active optimization config for the scope below and start an apply job to update workers.”
- Blast radius label: “Affects production traffic.” (only if prod)
- Type-to-confirm label: “Type ROLLBACK to continue”

2) Rollback started toast
- “Rollback started. Tracking job {job_id}.”

3) Rollback completed toast
- “Rollback completed. Active version is now v{target_version}.”

4) Rollback completed with warnings
- “Rollback completed with warnings. Some workers took longer to converge.” (link to details)

5) Rollback failed
- “Rollback failed to complete. Active pointer may have changed, but some workers did not converge.” (link to details + runbook)

Open questions (need decisions)
1) Concurrency semantics
- If apply is in progress, does rollback auto-cancel apply? (preferred)
- Who wins if both are requested within seconds? Backend likely decides; UX must align.

2) Gating behavior during rollback
- Do we gate rollback progression? Or only observe and warn?
- On-call feedback so far: rollback must not be blocked by gates, but we must surface if rollback increases 5xx.

3) Definition of “one-click”
- For enterprise, we’re adding reason + type-to-confirm. Is that still “one-click”?
- PM messaging: we can say “one action in Console” while still having confirmation.

4) What’s the default rollback target?
- “Rollback to last known-good” button (single CTA) vs selecting a specific version.
- If we add “Rollback to last known-good”, we must define known-good precisely.

5) Partial rollout UX viability
- Can we actually roll back only canary group with current control plane design?
- If not supported, UX should simplify: rollback entire scope only.

6) Private deployment UX
- Do we show an in-Console rollback button that only changes desired state, or do we require operator workflow instructions?
- Align with Private docs/installer commands; avoid making Private look “broken.”

7) Audit event exposure
- Do we show full raw JSON payload in Console? (some customers ask for exact SIEM fields)
- Security concern: ensure no secrets/tokens; must be safe to display.

8) Scope selector complexity
- Should rollback always be launched from a “Scope context” (e.g., you pick tenant/model/region first) to reduce mistakes?
- Current timeline view is per config; we may need a persistent scope bar.

Notes from feedback (summarized)
- SRE: wants rollback action reachable in <10 seconds during an incident; minimize navigation depth; include “copy summary for Slack”.
- Security/Naomi: reason + ticket link should be present (optional for internal?) but must be in audit events.
- Console eng/Chloe + Hannah: avoid too many modal states; keep a single confirm modal + job detail page.
- Support: needs easy visibility of “active version” and “last change” when a customer pings (include in top of config page).

Next steps
- Kenji: convert modal structure into DES-213 copy variants + acceptance criteria.
- Paula: confirm decisions on (1) concurrency semantics, (2) rollback gating behavior, (3) partial rollout support.
- Chloe/Felix: sanity check feasibility of showing worker convergence + mixed-state warnings.
- Marcus/Naomi: confirm which fields are required in UI vs only in audit logs.
